title: God Has Prepared an Eternal Home
story:
A family was preparing to move into a new house.

Their old home had many happy memories. The children had grown up there, celebrated birthdays there, and played in the same rooms for many years.

Even though they loved their old home, they knew it was not their final destination.

One evening, the children visited the new house with their parents. It was still being prepared, but their parents explained what each room would become.

The children became excited as they imagined their new life there.

The old house was familiar, but the new home gave them something to look forward to.

Our life on earth can sometimes feel like that.

We become attached to our homes, possessions, routines, and the people around us. Yet the Bible reminds us that our present earthly life is not the whole story.

2 Corinthians 5:1 speaks of our earthly body as a temporary dwelling and reminds us that God has prepared an eternal home for His people.

This does not mean that our present life has no value.

Every day matters. Our relationships matter. Our work matters. The people we love matter. God has given us this life as a gift and calls us to live it faithfully.

But we should remember that this world is temporary.

There will be moments when our bodies become weak, circumstances change, people we love leave us, or familiar things are taken away.

During such times, the promise of an eternal home can give us hope.

Our future with God is not built on something that will decay or disappear.

God has prepared something lasting and eternal.

This truth can also change the way we live today.

Instead of placing all our hope in possessions, achievements, comfort, or success, we can invest our lives in things that have eternal value.

We can love people, serve God, show kindness, forgive others, and remain faithful even when life is difficult.

If you are going through a season of uncertainty or loss, remember that your story does not end with what you can see today.

God has prepared an eternal home for His people.

Let that promise give you courage to live faithfully today and hope for tomorrow.
life_lesson: Our earthly life is temporary, but God has prepared an eternal home for His people. Live faithfully today without placing your ultimate hope in things that will pass away.
prayer:
Dear Heavenly Father,

Thank You for giving me the hope of an eternal home with You.

Help me remember that this earthly life is temporary and that my future is secure in Your hands.

When I become too attached to possessions, success, comfort, or temporary things, remind me of what has eternal value.

Help me appreciate the life You have given me and use each day faithfully for Your glory.

When I face weakness, loss, uncertainty, or change, strengthen my heart with the hope of eternity.

Help me love people, serve others, forgive freely, and live in a way that reflects Your kingdom.

Teach me not to fear the future because You have prepared a lasting home for those who belong to You.

Give me courage to face difficult seasons and faith to keep walking with You.

May the hope of eternity shape the way I live, the choices I make, and the way I treat others today.

Thank You that what You have prepared for Your people is eternal and cannot be destroyed.

In Jesus' name,
Amen.
reflection_question:
Are you placing too much of your hope and security in things that are temporary?

How does the promise of an eternal home change the way you look at difficulties in this life?

What can you do today that has lasting spiritual and eternal value?
verse: For we know that if the earthly tent we live in is destroyed, we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands.
